ladder.title: Distinct differences bound
ladder.q:
A set $A$ of positive integers is a Sidon set if all sums $a+b$ with $a\le b$ and $a,b\in A$ are distinct.

Let $A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\}$ be a Sidon set. Show that the positive differences $a-a'$ with $a,a'\in A$, $a>a'$, are pairwise distinct, and deduce that $|A|<\sqrt{2N}+1$.
ladder.source: Halberstam & Roth, Sequences, Vol. I (1966); K. O'Bryant, A complete annotated bibliography of work related to Sidon sequences, Electron. J. Combin. Dynamic Survey DS11 (2004)
ladder.note: The trivial upper bound; the whole of Erdős #30 is about replacing $\sqrt{2N}$ by $\sqrt N$ plus the smallest possible error.

ladder.title: The greedy Sidon sequence grows at most cubically
ladder.q:
Let $a_1=1$ and, for $n\ge1$, let $a_{n+1}$ be the least integer greater than $a_n$ such that $\{a_1,\ldots,a_{n+1}\}$ is a Sidon set.

Show that $a_{n+1}\le 4n^3$ for every $n\ge1$, and deduce that there is an absolute constant $c>0$ such that the infinite Sidon set $A=\{a_1,a_2,\ldots\}$ satisfies $|A\cap\{1,\ldots,N\}|\ge cN^{1/3}$ for all $N\ge1$.
ladder.source: Halberstam & Roth, Sequences, Vol. I (1966); O'Bryant, Electron. J. Combin. Dynamic Survey DS11 (2004)
ladder.note: This is exactly the greedy (Mian–Chowla) sequence of Erdős #340; the cubic bound $N^{1/3}$ is all that is known for it, against the conjectured $N^{1/2-\varepsilon}$.

ladder.title: The Erdős–Turán quadratic-residue construction
ladder.q:
Let $p$ be an odd prime and, for $0\le k<p$, let $r_k\in\{0,1,\ldots,p-1\}$ be the residue of $k^2$ modulo $p$. Show that
$$A_p=\{\,2pk+r_k : 0\le k<p\,\}$$
is a Sidon set of $p$ elements contained in $\{0,1,\ldots,2p^2-1\}$.

Deduce, using that the ratio of consecutive primes tends to $1$, that the maximum size $h(N)$ of a Sidon set in $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ satisfies $h(N)\ge(1/\sqrt2-o(1))\sqrt N$.
ladder.source: P. Erdős and P. Turán, On a problem of Sidon in additive number theory, and on some related problems, J. London Math. Soc. 16 (1941)
ladder.note: The first algebraic construction: it shows $h(N)$ really has order $\sqrt N$, leaving only the constant and the error term.

ladder.title: Lindström's upper bound
ladder.q:
Show that every Sidon set $A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\}$ satisfies
$$|A|<N^{1/2}+N^{1/4}+1.$$
ladder.source: B. Lindström, An inequality for B2-sequences, J. Combinatorial Theory 6 (1969); the bound $\sqrt N+O(N^{1/4})$ goes back to Erdős and Turán (1941)
ladder.note: Counting differences in short windows replaces $\sqrt{2N}$ by $\sqrt N$; the $N^{1/4}$ error term is the barrier Erdős #30 asks to break.

ladder.title: Singer difference sets give asymptotically optimal Sidon sets
ladder.q:
Let $q$ be a prime power. Show that there exist $q+1$ residues modulo $m=q^2+q+1$ such that every nonzero residue modulo $m$ is a difference of two of them in exactly one way.

Deduce that $h(q^2+q+1)\ge q+1$, where $h(N)$ is the maximum size of a Sidon subset of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$, and, using that consecutive primes $p<p'$ satisfy $p'/p\to1$, that $h(N)=(1+o(1))\sqrt N$.
ladder.source: J. Singer, A theorem in finite projective geometry and some applications to number theory, Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 43 (1938)
ladder.note: Matches the upper bound to first order; at $N=q^2+q+1$ it gives $h(N)\ge\sqrt N+1/2-o(1)$, and Green's Problem 31 asks whether one can beat $\sqrt N+O(1)$ even for infinitely many $N$.

ladder.title: B3 sets: counting bound and the Bose–Chowla construction
ladder.q:
Call $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ a $B_3$ set if the sums $a+b+c$ with $a\le b\le c$ and $a,b,c\in A$ are all distinct, and let $f(N)$ be the maximum size of a $B_3$ set in $\{1,\ldots,N\}$.

(a) By counting the sums, show that $f(N)<(18N)^{1/3}$.

(b) Show that for every prime power $q$ there is a $B_3$ set of $q$ integers contained in $\{1,\ldots,q^3-1\}$, and deduce that $f(N)\ge(1-o(1))N^{1/3}$.
ladder.source: R. C. Bose and S. Chowla, Theorems in the additive theory of numbers, Comment. Math. Helv. 37 (1962/63)
ladder.note: Gives the right order $N^{1/3}$ for triple sums; Erdős #241 asks whether the lower bound is asymptotically sharp, which needs an upper bound of the form $(1+o(1))N^{1/3}$.

ladder.title: Infinite Sidon sets cannot be dense at every scale
ladder.q:
Let $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ be an infinite Sidon set. Show that there is an absolute constant $C$ (independent of $A$) such that
$$\liminf_{x\to\infty}\frac{|A\cap[1,x]|}{\sqrt{x/\log x}}\le C.$$
In particular $\liminf_{x\to\infty}|A\cap[1,x]|/\sqrt x=0$.
ladder.source: Erdős; see Halberstam & Roth, Sequences, Vol. I (1966)
ladder.note: An infinite Sidon set must be thinner than finite optimal ones infinitely often; Erdős #1191 asks whether the constant $C$ can be replaced by $0$.

ladder.title: Maximal Sidon sets: the cube-root bound and Ruzsa's construction
ladder.q:
A Sidon set $A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\}$ is maximal if $A\cup\{x\}$ is not a Sidon set for every $x\in\{1,\ldots,N\}\setminus A$.

(a) Show that there is an absolute constant $c>0$ such that every maximal Sidon set $A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\}$ has $|A|\ge cN^{1/3}$.

(b) Show that there is an absolute constant $C$ such that for every large $N$ there is a maximal Sidon set $A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\}$ with $|A|\le C(N\log N)^{1/3}$.
ladder.source: Part (a): folklore, see P. Erdős, A. Sárközy and V. T. Sós, On sum sets of Sidon sets I, J. Number Theory (1994). Part (b): I. Z. Ruzsa, A small maximal Sidon set, Ramanujan J. 2 (1998)
ladder.note: The two bounds differ only by $(\log N)^{1/3}$; Erdős #156 asks whether that logarithm can be removed.

ladder.title: Ruzsa's dense infinite Sidon sequence
ladder.q:
Show that there is an infinite Sidon set $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ such that for every $\varepsilon>0$,
$$|A\cap\{1,\ldots,N\}|\ge N^{\sqrt2-1-\varepsilon}$$
for all sufficiently large $N$.
ladder.source: I. Z. Ruzsa, An infinite Sidon sequence, J. Number Theory 68 (1998)
ladder.note: Improves the greedy exponent $1/3$ (and Ajtai–Komlós–Szemerédi's $(N\log N)^{1/3}$, 1981) to $\sqrt2-1\approx0.414$; Erdős #39 asks for every exponent below $1/2$.

ladder.title: Balogh–Füredi–Roy: improving the constant in the N^{1/4} term
ladder.q:
Show that for all sufficiently large $N$, every Sidon set $A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\}$ satisfies
$$|A|\le\sqrt N+0.998\,N^{1/4}.$$
ladder.source: J. Balogh, Z. Füredi and S. Roy, An upper bound on the size of Sidon sets, arXiv:2103.15850 (2021); Amer. Math. Monthly (2023)
ladder.note: The first improvement of the constant $1$ in Lindström's $N^{1/4}$ term in over fifty years; Erdős #30 asks to lower the exponent $1/4$ itself to any $\varepsilon>0$.

ladder.title: The representation function is never eventually constant
ladder.q: Let $A\subseteq\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$ be infinite and let $r(n)=\#\{(a,b)\in A^2: a+b=n\}$ count ordered pairs. Show that $r(n)$ is not constant for all sufficiently large $n$.
ladder.source: P. Erdős and P. Turán, J. London Math. Soc. 16 (1941); the short parity proof is due to Dirac, as recounted in P. Erdős, Problems and results in additive number theory, Colloque sur la Théorie des Nombres, Bruxelles (1956)
ladder.note: The weakest form of the Erdős–Turán philosophy that a representation function cannot be too regular.

ladder.title: A basis of order two has at least square-root growth
ladder.q:
Let $A\subseteq\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$ be such that every sufficiently large integer can be written as $a+b$ with $a,b\in A$. Show that
$$\liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac{|A\cap\{0,1,\ldots,N\}|}{\sqrt N}\ge\sqrt2.$$
ladder.source: Folklore; see Halberstam & Roth, Sequences, Vol. I (1966)
ladder.note: Shows a basis of order $2$ has on average at least a constant number of representations, the starting point of the Erdős–Turán conjecture.

ladder.title: A thin basis from binary digits
ladder.q: Let $E$ be the set of nonnegative integers whose binary expansion uses only the powers $4^j$ ($j\ge0$), and let $O=2E$ be the set of those using only the powers $2\cdot4^j$. Show that $A=E\cup O$ satisfies $A+A\supseteq\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$ and $|A\cap\{0,1,\ldots,N\}|\le4\sqrt N$ for every $N\ge1$.
ladder.source: Folklore; see Halberstam & Roth, Sequences, Vol. I (1966)
ladder.note: The square-root lower bound is attained up to a constant, so the Erdős–Turán conjecture cannot follow from counting alone; in this example $r(n)$ is unbounded.

ladder.title: Schnirelmann's inequality
ladder.q:
For $A\subseteq\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$ let $A(n)=\#\{a\in A:1\le a\le n\}$ and define the Schnirelmann density $\sigma(A)=\inf_{n\ge1}A(n)/n$.

(a) Show that if $0\in A$ and $0\in B$ then $\sigma(A+B)\ge\sigma(A)+\sigma(B)-\sigma(A)\sigma(B)$.

(b) Deduce that if $0\in A$ and $\sigma(A)>0$, then $A$ is a basis of finite order: there is $h$ such that every nonnegative integer is a sum of $h$ elements of $A$.
ladder.source: M. B. Nathanson, Additive Number Theory: The Classical Bases, Graduate Texts in Mathematics 164 (1996)
ladder.note: The basic density-increment inequality for sumsets, the tool behind Schnirelmann's proof that the primes form a basis of finite order.

ladder.title: Erdős's covering-congruence obstruction for 2^k + p
ladder.q:
(a) Show that every integer $k$ lies in at least one of the residue classes $0 \bmod 2$, $0 \bmod 3$, $1 \bmod 4$, $3 \bmod 8$, $7 \bmod 12$, $23 \bmod 24$.

(b) Prove that there is an infinite arithmetic progression of odd positive integers none of which can be written as $2^k+p$ with $k\ge0$ an integer and $p$ a prime.
ladder.source: P. Erdős, On integers of the form 2^k + p and some related problems, Summa Brasil. Math. 2 (1950)
ladder.note: Contrasts with Romanoff's theorem (1934) that the integers $2^k+p$ have positive lower density; Erdős #16 asks whether such progressions explain all exceptions.

ladder.title: Erdős's density increment for adding a basis
ladder.q:
Let $\sigma$ denote Schnirelmann density, $\sigma(A)=\inf_{n\ge1}\#\{a\in A:1\le a\le n\}/n$. Let $B\subseteq\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$ with $0\in B$ be a basis of order $k$, i.e. every nonnegative integer is a sum of $k$ elements of $B$. Let $A\subseteq\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$ with $0\in A$ and $\alpha=\sigma(A)$. Show that
$$\sigma(A+B)\ge\alpha+\frac{\alpha(1-\alpha)}{2k}.$$
ladder.source: P. Erdős, On the arithmetical density of the sum of two sequences, one of which forms a basis for the integers, Acta Arith. 1 (1936)
ladder.note: This is Erdős #35 with $2k$ in place of $k$; the sharper form follows from Plünnecke's inequality $\sigma(A+B)\ge\alpha^{1-1/k}$ (J. Reine Angew. Math. 243, 1970).

ladder.title: A basis of order two with logarithmically many representations
ladder.q:
Let $r(n)=\#\{(a,b)\in A^2:a+b=n\}$. Show that there exist $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ and constants $0<c_1<c_2$ such that
$$c_1\log n\le r(n)\le c_2\log n$$
for all sufficiently large $n$.
ladder.source: P. Erdős, Problems and results in additive number theory, Colloque sur la Théorie des Nombres, Bruxelles (1956); extended to every order $h$ by P. Erdős and P. Tetali, Random Structures Algorithms 1 (1990)
ladder.note: Shows the conjectured growth $\log n$ in the strong Erdős–Turán conjecture is attainable; Erdős #66 asks whether $r(n)/\log n$ can even converge to a nonzero limit.

ladder.title: Bases of order two have a representation count of at least 8 infinitely often
ladder.q: Let $A\subseteq\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$ and $r(n)=\#\{(a,b)\in A^2:a+b=n\}$ (ordered pairs). Suppose $r(n)\ge1$ for every integer $n\ge0$. Show that $r(n)\ge8$ for infinitely many $n$.
ladder.source: P. Borwein, S. Choi and F. Chu, An old conjecture of Erdős–Turán on additive bases, Math. Comp. 75 (2006); improving the bound 6 of Grekos, Haddad, Helou and Pihko (J. Number Theory, 2003)
ladder.note: The best known constant lower bound on $\limsup r(n)$; Erdős #28 asks for $\limsup r(n)=\infty$.

ladder.title: The Erdős–Fuchs theorem
ladder.q:
Let $A\subseteq\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$ be infinite and let $R(N)=\#\{(a,b)\in A^2:a+b\le N\}$. Show that for no constant $c>0$ can one have
$$R(N)=cN+o\!\left(N^{1/4}(\log N)^{-1/2}\right)\quad(N\to\infty).$$
ladder.source: P. Erdős and W. H. J. Fuchs, On a problem of additive number theory, J. London Math. Soc. 31 (1956)
ladder.note: Quantifies that the representation function cannot be regular on average, answering a question of Erdős and Turán about $R(N)=cN+O(1)$; the analytic method is a model for attacks on the irregularity problems around Erdős #28 and #66.

ladder.title: Gallagher: a prime plus boundedly many powers of 2
ladder.source: P. X. Gallagher, Primes and powers of 2, Invent. Math. 29 (1975)
ladder.note: The density version of Erdős #10; the open problem asks for a single $k$ that represents all large integers.

ladder.title: Van der Waerden number W(3,2)
ladder.q: Show that every colouring of $\{1,2,\ldots,9\}$ with two colours contains a monochromatic $3$-term arithmetic progression, and that this fails for $\{1,2,\ldots,8\}$.
ladder.source: R. L. Graham, B. L. Rothschild and J. H. Spencer, Ramsey Theory (2nd ed., 1990)
ladder.note: The smallest nontrivial case of van der Waerden's theorem, of which Szemerédi's theorem is the density version.

ladder.title: Monotone 3-term progressions in permutations
ladder.q:
A monotone $k$-term arithmetic progression in a sequence $x_1,x_2,\ldots$ is a choice of indices $i_1<\cdots<i_k$ such that $x_{i_1},\ldots,x_{i_k}$ is an arithmetic progression (increasing or decreasing).

(a) Show that for every $n\ge1$ there is a permutation of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ with no monotone $3$-term arithmetic progression.

(b) Show that every permutation $x_1,x_2,\ldots$ of the positive integers contains a monotone $3$-term arithmetic progression.
ladder.source: J. A. Davis, R. C. Entringer, R. L. Graham and G. J. Simmons, On permutations containing no long arithmetic progressions, Acta Arith. 34 (1977/78)
ladder.note: The same paper constructs a permutation of $\mathbb{N}$ with no monotone $5$-term progression, leaving $4$ terms as Erdős #196.

ladder.title: A progression-free set from ternary digits
ladder.q: Let $r_3(N)$ be the maximum size of a subset of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ containing no three distinct elements in arithmetic progression. Show that the set of $n\ge1$ such that $n-1$ has only digits $0$ and $1$ in base $3$ contains no $3$-term arithmetic progression, and deduce that $r_3(N)\ge\tfrac12N^{\log2/\log3}$ for all $N\ge1$.
ladder.source: P. Erdős and P. Turán, On some sequences of integers, J. London Math. Soc. 11 (1936)
ladder.note: The first construction in the paper that introduced $r_k(N)$; it shows progression-free sets can have polynomial size.

ladder.title: Behrend's construction
ladder.q:
Show that there is a constant $c>0$ such that for all $N\ge2$ there is a set $A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\}$ with no $3$-term arithmetic progression and
$$|A|\ge N\exp\!\left(-c\sqrt{\log N}\right).$$
ladder.source: F. A. Behrend, On sets of integers which contain no three terms in arithmetical progression, Proc. Nat. Acad. Sci. USA 32 (1946)
ladder.note: Shows $r_3(N)=N^{1-o(1)}$, so any upper bound must leave room for this; it is still essentially the best lower bound.

ladder.title: Roth's theorem
ladder.q: Show that there is a constant $C$ such that for all $N\ge3$ every subset of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ with no $3$-term arithmetic progression has at most $CN/\log\log N$ elements.
ladder.source: K. F. Roth, On certain sets of integers, J. London Math. Soc. 28 (1953)
ladder.note: The $k=3$ case of Erdős #139 by Fourier-analytic density increment, the method all later 3-AP bounds refine.

ladder.title: Szemerédi's theorem
ladder.q: Let $k\ge3$ and let $r_k(N)$ be the maximum size of a subset of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ with no $k$-term arithmetic progression. Show that $r_k(N)=o(N)$ as $N\to\infty$; equivalently, every subset of $\mathbb{N}$ of positive upper density contains arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions.
ladder.source: E. Szemerédi, On sets of integers containing no k elements in arithmetic progression, Acta Arith. 27 (1975)
ladder.note: Settles Erdős #139 qualitatively; all later work is about the rate in $r_k(N)=o(N)$.

ladder.title: Gowers's quantitative Szemerédi theorem
ladder.q: Let $k\ge3$ and $c_k=2^{-2^{k+9}}$. Show that for all sufficiently large $N$, every subset of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ with no $k$-term arithmetic progression has at most $N(\log\log N)^{-c_k}$ elements.
ladder.source: W. T. Gowers, A new proof of Szemerédi's theorem, Geom. Funct. Anal. 11 (2001)
ladder.note: The first bound for all $k$ with a reasonable rate, introducing the Gowers uniformity norms.

ladder.title: Kelley–Meka bounds for 3-term progressions
ladder.q:
Show that there is a constant $c>0$ such that for all $N\ge2$ every subset of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ with no $3$-term arithmetic progression has at most
$$N\exp\!\left(-c(\log N)^{1/12}\right)$$
elements. Deduce that every $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ with $\sum_{n\in A}1/n=\infty$ contains a $3$-term arithmetic progression.
ladder.source: Z. Kelley and R. Meka, Strong bounds for 3-progressions, arXiv:2302.05537 (2023), FOCS 2023; exponent improved to 1/9 by T. F. Bloom and O. Sisask, arXiv:2302.07211 (2023)
ladder.note: Answers Green's Problem 9 and the $k=3$ case of Erdős #3, and brings the upper bound to the same shape as Behrend's lower bound, with exponent $1/12$ against $1/2$.

ladder.title: Leng–Sah–Sawhney bounds for long progressions
ladder.q:
Let $k\ge5$. Show that there is a constant $c_k>0$ such that for all sufficiently large $N$, every subset of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ with no $k$-term arithmetic progression has at most
$$N\exp\!\left(-(\log\log N)^{c_k}\right)$$
elements.
ladder.source: J. Leng, A. Sah and M. Sawhney, Improved bounds for Szemerédi's theorem, arXiv:2402.17995 (2024)
ladder.note: The first bound for $k\ge5$ beating every power of $\log\log N$; Erdős #3 for $k$-term progressions would follow from a bound $r_k(N)\ll N/(\log N)^{1+\delta}$ for some $\delta>0$.

ladder.title: The Green–Tao theorem
ladder.q: Show that for every $k\ge3$ the primes contain a $k$-term arithmetic progression.
ladder.source: B. Green and T. Tao, The primes contain arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions, Ann. of Math. 167 (2008)
ladder.note: A relative Szemerédi theorem for the primes, which have density zero; Erdős #141 asks for such progressions among consecutive primes, and #200 for the length of the longest one below $N$.
